title: Finally give it a try and make my first real AI game: Baba Yaga - Bodycam FPS
author: khiemngs
selftext:
So, half-professional game dev. After all the hype, i finnaly have time to give AI a try. So, I have this idea long time ago. Want to make Bodycam gameplay but with John Wick theme (my fav movie though). I did some smaller prototype with AI before, but nothing serious. This time, i want make it real.

Development times is 5 days, mostly using Opus 5.5.  
  
The first playable be done just in first day, but just gameplay, camera effect, and look boring.  
  
So, next 2 days, I use some free models for main  character, and cost tons of my times to chat and ask AI fix bones and do properly animtion. One things i learnt, use short video reference is best for AI to matching good animtion than tell them just words and expect it done well.

Using three.js as most of people recommended. But it dont have built-in editor to for debug and modifying things. But I am kind of using AI making small dev tool, so I make an animation editor, tons of debug panel (level jump, performance, rendering list, AI behaviour list, etc...) that really help me tune the game.

Next day of development is mostly modifing things, small details, video player like UI, the story (I come up with the ideas and direction how narrative is, AI make the details writing and code it).

Last day is for optimization and playtesting, making trailer myself (tried AI one shot prompt with my brief but dont feel good at all), setup itch page and got confidence enough to release it, ask friends to play.

What a journey, AI really boost the speed from a concept crunky idea to a real games (off course, for commercial I think it will need tons of work from human to make it perfect). I am no longer coding all the days as before, and this AI help me close the gap between idea in my head and real prototype.

  
You can play it here: [Baba Yaga by sKhiem](https://skhiem.itch.io/baba-yaga)

comments.author: typetwocarrier
comments.body:
This is a perfect mix of the indie vibes and the Bodycam PTSD. Give it a full destruction environment and this is a win-win. 

One thing to note - I see places where you had to squees fixes out of the model. Small lifehack - switch the model once you feel the "token drain" situation. Opus and Sonnet here and there give a better results.
